[3] The Transformer keeps this overall architecture but uses “stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers” in both the encoder and decoder instead of RNNs or CNNs. [3] The paper also says this attention-only design allows modeling dependencies “without regard to their distance” and enables “significantly more parallelization.” [1]  

I can’t say more about the exact internal transduction details beyond what the report states.

Analyze Transformer global dependency modeling via pure self-attn, excluding RNN/CNN transduction.

testCases.actualOutput:
The report says the Transformer was proposed as a model architecture that “eschew[s] recurrence” and “rely[ies] entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.” [3] It also states that the Transformer is “based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.” [4] More specifically, it is described as “the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.” [2]

The evidence also explains why this matters for dependency modeling: attention mechanisms allow modeling of dependencies “without regard to their distance in the input or output sequences,” whereas sequential computation imposes a fundamental constraint. [3] Self-attention is defined as relating different positions of a single sequence to compute a representation of the sequence. [1]

The report additionally notes a tradeoff: self-attention reduces the number of operations needed to relate distant positions to a constant number, but this comes “at the cost of reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions,” which the Transformer counteracts with Multi-Head Attention. [1]

In short, based on the report, the Transformer models global dependencies by using pure self-attention instead of RNNs or CNNs, enabling distance-independent dependency modeling and greater parallelization. [3][4]

The Transformer models global dependencies using only self-attention, without sequence-aligned RNNs or CNNs. In this architecture, encoder and decoder representations are computed through stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers, where each position can directly attend to all relevant positions in the sequence.

Why this helps:
- **Global dependency modeling:** self-attention relates any two positions directly, regardless of distance.
- **Short path length:** self-attention has **maximum path length O(1)**, compared with **O(n)** for recurrent layers and **O(log_k(n))** for convolutional layers, making long-range dependencies easier to learn.
- **Parallelization:** self-attention requires only **O(1)** sequential operations per layer, while recurrent layers require **O(n)**, so it supports much more parallel computation.
- **No recurrence/convolution needed:** the paper states the Transformer is the first transduction model to rely entirely on self-attention for input/output representations.

Because self-attention alone does not encode order, the Transformer adds **positional encodings** to embeddings, using sinusoidal functions so the model can still capture token positions and potentially generalize to longer sequences.
